raw_response:
I've been farming these 40 mu in Quzhou for 30 years now. At 58, I'm not as strong as I used to be, and it's just me at home since my wife passed and the kids went to work in Shijiazhuang. So I have to be smart about labor. I use machines where I can, and I hire people for the jobs I can't handle alone — especially cotton picking and the wheat harvest.

I put 30 mu in wheat-maize double crop. That's my bread and butter. Even if one crop has a bad year, the other usually carries me through. The other 10 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton is a lot of work, especially now that I'm older, but the price has been decent and my neighbor Old Wang did well with it last year, so I'm keeping it.

**Winter wheat** — I planted this last October with an improved variety, about 30 jin per mu. Cost me roughly 30 yuan per mu for the seed. Before planting I did rotary tillage and put down 80 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — the 18-22-5 type. The extension office says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've been doing this long enough to know my land needs a bit more. So with the basal compound and about 10 kg of urea topdress at jointing, I'm at roughly 19 kg nitrogen per mu. I'll irrigate three times: winter irrigation if it's dry, once at green-up around March, and once at heading in May. Water costs keep going up — the meter on the well never stops — so I watch that carefully. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and I keep an eye out for aphids and rust. Expecting about 450 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**Summer maize** — I'll plant Denghai hybrid right after wheat harvest in mid-June. Window is tight, sometimes only five or six days, so I use no-tillage planting with my machine. Saves time and diesel. Seed costs about 55 yuan per mu now. I put 80 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, the 28-6-6 formula. That's usually enough for the whole season — the soil still has some fertility from the wheat. I might irrigate twice if July is dry, but sometimes once is enough. Maize doesn't need much spraying — herbicide at planting and maybe one insecticide spray if the armyworms show up. Hoping for 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton** — I plant guoxinmian around April 20th on 10 mu. I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — I use the 15-15-15 general formula. Then I topdress another 50 jin when it starts flowering. That's about 15 kg nitrogen per mu total. Cotton needs a lot of pesticide. I spray for weeds once, and for aphids and bollworm maybe 8 to 10 times through the summer. I irrigate twice, usually in July and August. The biggest cost is labor — I hire women from the village for the picking in September and October, and for the pruning too. That runs me a good chunk of cash, but I can't do all that bending and picking myself anymore at my age. I'm hoping for around 280 kg per mu.

All told, my cash costs this year will be about 28,500 yuan. That's a big chunk of my savings, but I keep some cash reserve for doctor visits or machine repairs. I'd rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad yield — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps. If prices don't crash and we don't get a drought, I should come out okay.
